items.proposed_resolution: Accepted with clarification: do not hardcode provider/model names or exact default models. Canonical Plans define capability lanes and role contracts; Settings binds each lane to the user's configured providers/accounts/model profiles. If no configured profile satisfies a required lane, surface a settings/configuration blocker rather than silently selecting an arbitrary model.
items.remaining_choice: User may later configure provider/model profiles in Settings. No named default provider/model is required for Plan compile.

items.compile_effect: Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md, Plans/Run_Graph_View.md, Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md, Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, Plans/Widget_System.md, Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md, Plans/Wiring_Matrix.md, Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/chain-wizard.md, and Plans/chain-wizard-flexibility.md should be updated/audited.
items.proposed_resolution: Keep Orchestrator six-tab spine and add Goal/WorkGraph overlays instead of inventing a wholly separate Orchestrator page family. Use header for GoalRun status/authority/cost/certification; Progress for Goal tree, WorkNodes and subagent waves; Seams for owner/write-boundary/lease state; Node Graph for WorkGraph dependencies and verification overlays; Evidence for receipts/validators/findings; History for events/replans/repair cycles; Ledger for source mapping and compile lineage. Add side drawers for subagents and verification details. Settings receives dedicated capability-lane, subagent policy, verification policy, write policy, and Goal Mode policy panels.
items.remaining_choice: Exact pixel layout, component styling, and tab microcopy remain GUI implementation choices once FinalGUISpec accepts the surface contracts.

items.compile_effect: Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md owns compiler contract. Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md and Plans/Executor_Protocol.md consume runtime objects without bypassing scheduler truth. Plans/Contracts_V0.md should define object contracts/ContractRefs.
items.proposed_resolution: Define an Orchestrator-facing WorkGraph/WorkNode runtime contract now, but keep executable NodeSeed/WorkNode generation gated behind Plan_To_Node_Compilation. For this feature, canonical Plans should specify data shapes and boundaries: GoalRun, WorkGraph, WorkNode, SubagentWave, VerificationCycle, DefectBundle, RepairWorkNode, WorkNodeReceipt, GoalCompletionReceipt, CapabilityLane, and CertificationTier. PlanUnit index remains source; NodeSeed is a generated candidate artifact; WorkNode is only executable after compiler readiness, existence, dependency, acceptance, permission, and scheduler gates pass.
items.remaining_choice: Exact generated artifact schemas and compiler output paths remain future-facing until Plan_To_Node_Compilation is explicitly implemented.

items.compile_effect: State/verification_repair_loop_contract.json already records this; canonical Plans should propagate it to Orchestrator, Goal Runtime, Executor/Run modes, and Settings verification policy.
items.proposed_resolution: Retain the current default: same defect signature fails twice triggers strategy adjustment; third failed cycle triggers high-end adjudicator/root-cause replan. Always rerun verification after repair. Never mark done with known findings. Keep thresholds configurable by verification policy.
items.remaining_choice: Only change if Jared wants a different default threshold.

items.compile_effect: Compile goal should update state/doc_impact_matrix only if it remains a ledger artifact; canonical Plans should encode the policy that owner-doc rewrites require consumer/backlink audits.
items.proposed_resolution: Keep snapshot doc impact matrix as planning memory, but require compile goal to rerun a live backlink/reference audit before edits. Treat P0 docs as required update candidates, P1 docs as direct consumer/policy audit candidates, and P2 docs as stale-reference audit candidates. Do not treat snapshot counts as canonical if live repo differs.
items.remaining_choice: No product choice required; this is a compile-time safety rule.
items.topic: live backlink audit at compile time

items.proposed_resolution: Accepted with clarification: Requirements Doc Builder uses the ledger system while the user is talking through/designing requirements. After the conversational ledger is sufficiently complete, Doc Builder invokes invisible Goal Mode to convert the ledger into requirements docs with audit/verification. Goal_Runtime_System owns the engine-level invisible Goal behavior; Chain Wizard/Doc Builder docs own builder entry, activity, pause/cancel/resume, and document-production UX; Assistant Chat owns visible chat Goal Mode. Doc Builder invisible conversion goals are not default Orchestrator WorkNodes unless explicitly handed to Orchestrator execution.
items.remaining_choice: If a dedicated Requirements_Doc_Builder.md owner doc exists in the live repo, compile should prefer it for builder-specific behavior; otherwise chain-wizard-flexibility remains the owner. No product design blocker remains.
items.topic: Requirements Doc Builder invisible Goal owner placement

must_not_do: Do not reduce subagent usage; use bounded extensive subagents with cost-aware lanes.
Do not let low-end executors or subagents certify parent GoalRun completion.
Do not skip verification after repair.
Do not create executable WorkNodes/NodeSeeds before the compiler contract is complete.
Do not treat Chain Wizard or Doc Builder invisible goals as Orchestrator WorkNodes by default.
scope: Resolve deferred implementation/readiness items before canonical Plan compile where possible.
user_clarifications: Default model/provider values are not hardcoded and depend entirely on which providers/accounts/model profiles the user has configured.
Requirements Doc Builder uses the ledger during the conversational phase, then invisible Goal Mode converts the ledger into requirements docs.
